_comment: DRAFT — issue #23 preparation only. NOT wired into next.config.ts and must not be
until the full launch scope (#23's other acceptance criteria) is signed off.
Shape matches Next.js 16's `redirects()` config array exactly
(node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/03-api-reference/05-config/01-next-config-js/redirects.md):
each entry is { source, destination, permanent }. To wire this up at cutover, copy the
`entries` array into next.config.ts's `async redirects() { return [...] }` verbatim.
`permanent: true` emits a 308 (Next.js's permanent-redirect status, method-preserving)
rather than a literal 301 — functionally equivalent for SEO purposes (both signal
'cache this redirect permanently' to crawlers and browsers); flagging the distinction
since the issue calls this a '301 map' but Next.js doesn't emit literal 301s here.
Destinations are hardcoded to /es/... (not locale-relative) because the old WordPress
site had no CA/EN content — see docs/launch/301-map.md's rationale section.
Update (#79): aviso-legal-imprint, politica-de-cookies-ue, and declaracion-de-privacidad-ue
now point at real pages, upgraded to high confidence. Only accesibilidad remains a `_gap`
entry redirecting to home (`/es`) as a placeholder, per docs/launch/301-map.md's
content-parity-gap section — update it once a real accessibility page exists.
Not included here (needs no config): the bare '/' root, which already resolves via
proxy.ts's own locale detection with no explicit redirect needed. WWW/non-WWW and
HTTP/HTTPS are a Vercel domain-settings task at cutover, not a next.config concern —
see docs/launch/301-map.md.
